A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Antithetic Noise in Diffusion Models by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original correlation, image-diversity, uncertainty-estimation, and inverse-reconstruction experiments, with additional results and analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds results for further generative models, MRI reconstruction, image editing, guidance sensitivity, and partial noise negation.

M1.justification: The core antithetic sampling and MC/AMC/RQMC estimators remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 adds a FlowEdit adaptation that replaces two independent noises at each timestep with an antithetic pair before averaging velocity updates. V2's explicit K-noise construction implements a generalization already proposed in v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds ImageNet class-conditioned generation, LSUN-Cat and LSUN-Bedroom experiments, MNIST generation, fastMRI reconstruction, and text-guided image editing on 76 FlowEdit prompts. It removes motion deblurring, which v1 evaluated separately from Gaussian deblurring. The original CIFAR-10, CelebA-HQ, Church, and prompt benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly compares FlowEdit using independent internal noises against its antithetic variant. V2 Table 2 also adds AMC with k=8 alongside k=2, MC, and QMC. The principal independent-noise and Monte Carlo controls are retained; additional generative models and inverse solvers mainly serve as application backbones.

E3.justification: V2 adds dataset/class/prompt-centralized Pearson correlation and Wasserstein-distance evaluation. New protocols include 400 eight-noise batches at the retained 3,200-sample budget, one-step consistency-model evaluation, and 100 reconstruction pairs from one measurement using 50-step DDS. Existing pixel-statistic definitions and principal MC/AMC sample budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 adds guidance-scale sensitivity tests at scales 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9, partial upper-half noise-negation experiments, and Wasserstein-based checks of the correlation findings. These investigate conditioning sensitivity and spatial locality. The antisymmetry-score analysis and RQMC budget-allocation study already existed in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: V2 introduces t-tests for correlation comparisons and reports significance below 10^-10; its Wasserstein table includes standard deviations, t-statistics, and p-values. The main correlation table now reports means and standard deviations instead of extrema and quartiles. Existing confidence-interval constructions and the five repetitions of RQMC configurations are retained.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial correlation, k=8, DiT, MRI, and FlowEdit results. Reported CIFAR-10 diversity improvements change from 86.1422% to 88.78% for SSIM and from 8.2881% to 6.69% for LPIPS in corresponding tables. DPS confidence intervals are revised and motion-deblurring entries disappear. Standard DDPM correlations and antisymmetry-score results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendices A.2-A.4 develop Ornstein-Uhlenbeck score convergence, a one-step correlation bound, Hermite-expansion convergence, and preservation of orthogonal symmetries. Appendix A.6.1 adds MTP2 and curvature assumptions with one-step and global DDIM propositions. Existing MC/AMC proofs and the original FKG argument are retained and reorganized. Some new Hermite formulas omit required normalization factors.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claimed phenomenon beyond diffusion to VAEs and normalizing flows and add image-editing benefits. V2 also presents efficient inverse-solver benchmarking as a central application. The symmetry conjecture, up-to-90% narrower confidence intervals, and training-free, no-overhead characterization are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting centralization to removal of shared image structure, stronger guidance to increased similarity, and partial noise negation to localized spatial effects. It also uses the new convergence and symmetry-preservation arguments to strengthen the proposed mechanism. The unresolved conjecture and limited benefits for nonlinear perceptual metrics were already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-code link, an explicit K-noise generation recipe, consistency-model checkpoint identifiers, CFG scales, VAE/Glow implementation references, FlowEdit settings, and fastMRI provenance. The original GPU and generation-time information is relocated unchanged. Newly disclosed CFG values do not establish that retained experiments changed settings.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage expands to FlowEdit, DDS/InverseBench, epistemic-uncertainty studies, and OU/MTP2 foundations. Section 4 explicitly distinguishes the work from epistemic-uncertainty research. These are targeted extensions: the central positioning against task-specific noise optimization and the claimed first application of QMC to diffusion remain.

P1.justification: V2 substantially revises the abstract, contribution narrative, and experimental organization to prioritize uncertainty quantification. Diversity moves behind the inverse-problem applications; the main-text FKG discussion and MC proposition move into the appendices. The contents page is removed, references switch to author-year style, and explanatory sections are expanded.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are redesigned, the main correlation table is reorganized around models and two correlation metrics, and the experimental tables are restructured. V2 adds centralized-correlation tables, guidance and partial-negation plots, and DiT image grids. Existing symmetry plots and several qualitative grids are retained, while the bunny visualization is removed.

improvement.justification: Broader model validation, centralization checks, guidance and spatial analyses, and FlowEdit/MRI applications strengthen the empirical support for v1's generality claims. Added code-access information also helps reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removal of the low-gain motion-deblurring case, unreconciled CIFAR-10 centroid values in v2 Tables 2 and 11, and errors in new theoretical arguments, including Hermite normalization in Appendix A.3. The empirical and documentation gains support a limited net improvement.
